I am a man of 37 years, farming here in Rukwa where the rains come once a year from November to April. I never went to school, so I farm the way my father showed me and the way my neighbors do. My maize plot is big — about two and a half hectares — and I have other plots too, so I must spread my hands and my shillings across all of them. Fertilizer from the shop costs too much for a plot this size, and most men in my village do not buy it for maize; we save the small cash for seed and for hiring help at weeding time. I will put cattle manure where I can carry it, plant my own seed I kept from last harvest mixed in with beans between the rows, and call on a few young men from the village to help me weed when the maize is at the knee.
